# requireException

<link-summary>Returns the value as an `Exception`, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireException() — Returns the value as an `Exception`, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireException(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected an Exception."): Exception;
```

The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                           | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                             | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected an Exception."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`Exception` — the same value, typed as an `Exception`.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                        |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not an `Exception`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // => new IllegalArgumentException()
requireException(new Error()); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireException({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
